Bilateral thyroid nodules, provisionally classified as C-TIRADS category 3; one on the right is relatively large. Please correlate clinically. No obvious abnormality is seen in the bilateral parathyroid regions. No obvious abnormal lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral neck. (Explanation: C-TIRADS categories 1-2, probability of malignancy 0%; C-TIRADS category 3, probability of malignancy <2%; C-TIRADS category 4A, probability of malignancy 2-10%; C-TIRADS category 4B, probability of malignancy 10-50%; C-TIRADS category 4C, probability of malignancy 50-90%; C-TIRADS category 5, probability of malignancy >90%; C-TIRADS category 6, biopsy-proven malignant nodule. Modified C-TIRADS refers to the category after the risk level of a nodule has been modified based on the physician's experience or the medical history. Reference: Endocrine, 2120, 256-279)
Thyroid: The bilateral thyroid lobes are plump and irregular in contour, with smooth capsules and homogeneous internal echogenicity. Multiple predominantly cystic and predominantly solid nodules of varying sizes are seen within the parenchyma. The largest on the left measures 7.7 × 4.3 mm, and the largest on the right measures 40 × 28 mm (extending retrosternally). Elastography shows that the above nodules are soft to intermediate in stiffness, with elasticity scores of 2-3 points (using the 5-point scoring system). Coarse calcific hyperechoes are seen within some nodules. CDFI shows normal blood supply to the thyroid parenchyma. Elastography shows the stiffness of the thyroid parenchyma to be intermediate. No obvious space-occupying lesions are seen in the bilateral parathyroid regions. No obviously abnormal enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the bilateral neck. Three-dimensional ultrasonography shows no obvious abnormal distribution pattern in the gland or soft tissues. Three-dimensional color and power Doppler ultrasonography shows no large, tortuous vessels with a radial distribution on either sagittal or coronal planes.
